newsitem.title: USA: US WCoast light crudes extend losses with WTI late.
newsitem.headline: US WCoast light crudes extend losses with WTI late.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crude prices continued to lose ground late Monday, as West Texas Intermediate (WTI) ended 34 cents lower and saw further declines on ACCESS.
October WTI weakened on profit-taking and thin volume amidst a holiday on London's oil exchange.
Pricing for cash WTI switched to October, ending at $21.50/21.60 a barrel, versus September's $21.90/22.00 finish Friday. September values had been 25-30 cents over October.
All but one small buyer kept out of the market, with few sales expected ahead of the long holiday weekend next week.
Differentials for October Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude remained $2.05 a barrel below October WTI.
Traders forecast West Coast refiners to run full-out this autumn ahead of end-of-year and first-quarter maintenance.
Margins were also relatively good, they said, given WTI's recent fall.
Unocal Corp said the crude processor at its Carson, Calif., refinery ran at full capacity Monday following repairs late last week.
Prices for Line 63 slipped with WTI, and spot deals off WTI remained dormant.
Kern River and Wilmington grades were unchanged late.
